q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an FIBC jumbo bag?
title: FIBC jumbo bag carbon footprint per bag
short: Multiply the polypropylene fabric, webbing loops and liner per bag by the resin supplier's figure, then add tape extrusion, weaving, coating and stitching electricity. Divide the plant's energy by bags made.
audience: FIBC and bulk bag makers and exporters

ul: Polypropylene for tape, fabric and loops.

p: Report per bag by its safe working load and weight, since a 1,000 kg bag and a 2,000 kg bag use different fabric weights.

example.title: Worked example: FIBC jumbo bag unit per bag (one month)
lines: Plant total: 106,500 / 100,000 = 1.065 kg CO2 per bag
Add polypropylene for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
